thread:
incident-bot: PAGER: streaming-retail-prod — streaming-proxy latency spike. p95 ~3.2s (SLO 500ms), p99 ~9.1s. Multiple SSE/WebSocket clients reporting stalls and reconnects. Frontend errors increasing. Paging on-call @liz-oncall. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/streaming/stalls

liz-oncall: got it, I'm looking. Any customer tickets yet?

jordan-support: seeing a handful of 5xxs from a top customer (acme-inc). They report partial transcripts missing. Ticket #INC-8342.

ben-sre: quick triage — looks like proxy (edge) CPU in a few AZs hit 95% and connections piled up. Downstream inference pods healthy. Suspect slow clients/backpressure + proxy buffering + keepalive churn.

chris-eng: confirmed per-host accept queues growing. Envoy stats: conn_total rising, upstream_rq_time p95 spiked. Also saw SSE chunk queues high.

dana-ml: model latency fairly stable, KV cache hit rates unchanged. So not model-side.

ben-sre: mitigation plan: 1) throttle heavy streaming clients via rate-limit header (quick config), 2) reduce proxy buffering (disable proxy_response_buffering), 3) scale edge pool + shift traffic to healthy AZs, 4) enable immediate flush of chunks (proxy config). Rolling the proxy config first.

liz-oncall: Ben, do we have runbook steps? I'm paging ops-bot to execute scaling if needed.

ops-bot: runbook/streaming-tail invoked by @liz-oncall. Step 1: apply buffer disable on envoy config for streaming routes. Step 2: increase keepalive timeout on NLB. Step 3: scale edge-deployment by +30%.

ben-sre: applying config patch now (k8s):
```
kubectl -n edge patch configmap envoy-streaming --patch '{"data":{"proxy_response_buffering":"false","flush_interval_ms":"10"}}'
kubectl -n edge rollout restart deployment/edge-proxy
```

chris-eng: while the rollout happens, can we route traffic away from AZ-b where CPU is most saturated? I can update ringpop/traffic-router to drop to 0% for AZ-b.

ben-sre: doing gradual traffic shift +40% away from AZ-b -> AZ-a,c. Command: `trafficctl scale --from=az-b --to=az-a,az-c --pct=40 --grace=30s`

jordan-support: acme-inc on status page; mentioned they see reconnect loops and truncated chunks. They're asking ETA for fix.

liz-oncall: keep customer informed: "We're investigating streaming stalls and rerouting traffic, mitigation in progress. Next update in 15m."

evan-product: any risk to dedicated/dedicated customers? This is on hosted streaming proxies only right?

ben-sre: yes, only hosted edge pool. Dedicated clusters unaffected.

chris-eng: rollout shows new envoy pods with the buffer flag off. Observability: chunk-latency p95 dropping already from 3.2s -> 1.1s on the patched nodes. Connections per-host trending down.

dana-ml: monitoring p99 model token latency — still stable.

ops-bot: scaled edge-proxy deployment from 60 -> 78 pods in cluster edge-prod-us-east-1. Confirmed healthchecks passing.

ben-sre: posting quick grep of logs showing stalled chunk flush before patch:
```
[edge-proxy-123] stream_flush delayed 1200ms queued_chunks=42 client_write_err=null
[edge-proxy-123] accept queue growth: 102 -> 512
[envoy] outbound flush blocked by slow client fd=102
```

liz-oncall: nice. Any client-side workarounds we can recommend to customers (short term)?

chris-eng: ask them to enable chunk-ack/keepalive or reduce per-connection concurrency. For websockets suggest enabling application-level heartbeats every 10s to avoid long idle-backed buffers.

jordan-support: sending note to acme-inc with suggested temporary heartbeat and saying we're rolling fixes.

ben-sre: follow-up: set proxy idle timeouts longer to reduce teardown churn: `idle_timeout: 120s` (from 30s). Also tuning NLB TCP keepalive to 60s.

ops-bot: applied idle_timeout and keepalive.

chris-eng: after config + scale + routing, p95 now 480ms, p99 1.1s. Down from p95 3.2s, p99 9.1s. Still above SLO at p99, but materially improved.

liz-oncall: record impact: 12% of streaming sessions experienced stalls >5s during peak. Top affected customers: acme-inc, beta-shop, fast-sms. No data loss reported, intermittent partial chunks.

dana-ml: schedule a post-incident eval to see if prefix caching could reduce token pressure in bursts.

ben-sre: next steps before handoff: 1) keep mitigation configs for 60m, 2) observe p99, 3) if stable, gradually revert traffic routing and reduce extra pool size, 4) run a canary test for client backpressure handling.

liz-oncall: handing off to @chris-eng for overnight monitoring at 2312346720. Handoff summary:
- Root cause: edge proxy buffering + slow-client backpressure + AZ-b CPU saturation.
- Actions taken: disabled proxy buffering, enabled immediate chunk flush, increased idle_timeouts, scaled edge pool + traffic shift off AZ-b, NLB keepalive bump.
- Current status: partial mitigation — p95 within SLO, p99 improved but still ~1.1s. Ongoing monitoring and customer comms.
- Open tickets: INC-8342 (acme), RUNBOOK-STREAM-TAIL (actions taken).

chris-eng: ack, will monitor through night and escalate if p99 climbs >2s or error rate >1%. I'll run a synthetic streaming canary every 2m and report anomalies to this thread.

liz-oncall: great, thanks everyone. Closing pager for me. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Handoff logged — from liz-oncall to chris-eng at 2312346720. Incident severity: S2 (streaming degradation).

chris-eng: starting canary: `./canary --url wss://streaming.redwood.example --interval 120s --payload size=small`

jordan-support: I've updated status page and customers notified. Will follow-up with private notes to acme-inc's TAM.

ben-sre: I'll open a postmortem draft with timeline + mitigation options (proxy kernel tuning, adaptive flush heuristics, rate-limiter per-client). Assigning to @ben-sre and @chris-eng.

chris-eng: logging any follow-ups here. If anyone notices regressions ping me directly.

incident-bot: Incident note saved: 2312345678. Thank you for responding.
